title: Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals Stock Surges 19% After Triglyceride Drug Aces Two Phase 3 Trials
excerpt: Plozasiran delivered up to 81% triglyceride reduction and eliminated acute pancreatitis risk in patients with a history of the condition, putting Arrowhead on track for a broader FDA filing by year-end.
body:
• Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals' stock rose 19% to a five-year high of $88.70 following positive Phase 3 trial results for plozasiran.
  • Plozasiran demonstrated significant triglyceride reductions of 79% and 81% in the SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 trials, respectively.
  • The drug achieved a 100% reduction in acute pancreatitis events among patients with a history of the condition.
  • Arrowhead plans to seek broader FDA approval for plozasiran by the end of 2026, targeting severe hypertriglyceridemia.
Key Takeaways
  • Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals' stock surged 19% after plozasiran's Phase 3 trials showed significant triglyceride reductions.
  • Plozasiran achieved a 100% reduction in acute pancreatitis events in patients with a history of the condition.
  • Arrowhead plans to file for broader FDA approval by the end of 2026, targeting severe hypertriglyceridemia.
  • Plozasiran offers quarterly dosing, providing a convenience advantage over Ionis Pharmaceuticals' monthly treatment.

Plozasiran Delivers Blockbuster Phase 3 Results

Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals saw its stock rocket 19% on Wednesday, closing at $88.70 — a five-year high — after its triglyceride-lowering drug plozasiran posted strong results in two yearlong Phase 3 studies. The stock blew past its previous 52-week high of $87.83, up from a previous close of $74.52.

In the SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 trials, patients receiving 25 mg of plozasiran once every three months achieved median triglyceride reductions of 79% and 81%, respectively, after 12 months. The placebo group saw roughly 27% reduction. Both studies met their primary endpoints and achieved all prespecified secondary endpoints, according to the company.

The drug also delivered what Arrowhead called an "unprecedented" outcome on pancreatitis. Among patients with a history of acute pancreatitis — a painful and potentially fatal inflammation of the pancreas often triggered by high triglycerides — plozasiran produced a 100% reduction in events compared to placebo. Across the broader study population, the reduction was 78%.

"This is a best-case scenario for ARWR as they were able to hit the stats on acute pancreatitis despite a trial that was originally designed to just hit on triglycerides."

— Luca Issi, RBC Capital Markets analyst

Taking On Ionis in a Growing Market

Plozasiran already has FDA approval under the brand name Redemplo for familial chylomicronemia syndrome, a rare genetic lipid disorder. The SHASTA trials target a much larger patient population: adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia, a condition that raises cardiovascular disease risk and affects millions.

Arrowhead's main competitor is Ionis Pharmaceuticals, which was first to market with Tryngolza, its own triglyceride-lowering therapy. In clinical data, Tryngolza showed an 85% reduction in acute pancreatitis events across patients with or without a history of the condition. RBC's Issi noted that physicians are likely to view both drugs as comparably effective on pancreatitis outcomes.

Where plozasiran may gain an edge is dosing convenience. Tryngolza requires monthly injections; plozasiran is given quarterly. Issi also flagged that Tryngolza has been associated with increased liver fat — a signal not seen with plozasiran, which demonstrated a favorable safety profile with no new safety signals, no meaningful changes in liver health, and no cases of hypersensitivity or thrombocytopenia.

"IONS is first to market, but ARWR is poised to join the race with a drug that has shown a comparable benefit in AP and can offer a dosing advantage, and potentially spare the liver fat signal."

— Luca Issi, RBC Capital Markets analyst

Arrowhead said it plans to file a supplemental new drug application (sNDA) with the U.S. FDA by the end of 2026, using data from the SHASTA-3, SHASTA-4, and MUIR-3 trials. Detailed results from the two studies will be presented as a HOT LINE Late Breaker at the European Society of Cardiology Congress in Munich on Aug. 30, 2026.

Issi reiterated his outperform rating on ARWR with a price target of $87 — a level the stock has already exceeded. Wall Street consensus is broadly positive: of 14 analysts covering the stock, nine rate it a buy and one a strong buy, according to MarketBeat, with an average 12-month price target of $88.75.

What It Means for Investors

For biotech-focused investors, Wednesday's data represent a pivotal inflection point. Arrowhead has gone from a company with a niche approval to one with a credible shot at a blockbuster indication. Some retail investors on StockTwits speculated plozasiran could become a "$10 billion per year drug" if it captures significant share of the severe hypertriglyceridemia market.

Ionis Pharmaceuticals (IONS) closed up 1.2% at $54.01, a muted reaction that suggests the market sees room for both drugs. The key question going forward is whether plozasiran's quarterly dosing and cleaner liver-safety profile will be enough to erode Tryngolza's first-mover advantage as physicians gain more clinical experience with both therapies.

The ESC Congress presentation in August and the sNDA filing timeline will be the next major catalysts for ARWR shares.
